sourceIssues.locator: Theorem 4.19, function-field case, p.101 (with the definition of maximal variation, §1.6, p.16); the same statement is Theorem 4.19 in arXiv v4, p.100, in the author manuscript dated 21 August 2024 (126 pp., the journal's revision date; SHA-256 b36f4860…813e)
sourceIssues.printed: "Theorem 4.19. Let K be either a number field or a function field of one variable. Let S be a quasi-projective variety over K. Let π : X → S be a smooth relative curve over S of genus g > 1 with maximal variation. Let α be a line bundle on X of positive degree on fibers of π. Then the following morphisms satisfy the relative Bogomolov conjecture: (1) the S-morphism i_α^m : X^m_{/S} → J^m_{/S} for any m ≥ dim S + 1 …", where (§1.6) maximal variation means that the moduli morphism S → M_{g,R} is generically finite.
sourceIssues.correction: For a function field K of a curve over k, the hypothesis must be maximal variation of a model over k (equivalently, as the proof says, bigness of the relevant adelic line bundles over k rather than over K), which excludes isotrivial families. With that hypothesis, or for K a number field, the statement stands.
sourceIssues.reason: Counterexample to the function-field case: k algebraically closed of characteristic 0, K = k(t), S = Spec K, X = C₀ ×_k K for a smooth projective curve C₀/k of genus > 1, and α of degree 1. The moduli morphism Spec K → M_{g,K} is a point, hence generically finite, so X → S has maximal variation in the sense of §1.6. But every point of C₀(k) has canonical height 0 in the constant Jacobian, and these points are Zariski dense in X, so part (1) fails for m = 1 = dim S + 1; constant products give the same failure for the other parts. The proof itself notes that "we need the bigness of the adelic line bundles over k instead of over K", which a constant family does not have. The main uniform Bogomolov theorem excludes isotrivial families and is unaffected. Found by the extraction (items 185–189, 262–266).

review.reason: Confirmed. Theorem 4.19 and the definition of maximal variation are both verbatim in the same author manuscript the errata names: I re-fetched it from http://faculty.bicmr.pku.edu.cn/~yxy/preprints/bigness_and_bogomolov.pdf on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is b36f4860cc0f098ef062523e8a5147e8172d1e4e357fc76a63cd7c0d782a813e, reproducing the recorded hash, with the date 'August 21, 2024' on its title page, on pages 101 and 16, and the counterexample stands. With S = Spec K for K = k(t), the moduli morphism S → M_{g,K} is a K-point, which is quasi-finite on the dense open U = S, so §1.6's definition of maximal variation is satisfied vacuously; for X = C₀ ×_k K with C₀/k of genus g > 1 and α of degree 1, every point of C₀(k) has canonical height zero in the constant Jacobian and C₀(k) is Zariski dense, so part (1) fails at m = 1 = dim S + 1. What settles the diagnosis is that the proof on the same page says so itself: 'Similar to Proposition 4.18, we need the bigness of the adelic line bundles over k instead of over K, where k = Z if K is a number field and k is the field of constants if K is a function field of one variable.' A constant family does not have it. So the function-field case is false as printed — 'a stated result' is right — and the correction, maximal variation of a model over k, is what the proof needs.

sourceIssues.locator: §4.6.3, statement of the relative Bogomolov conjecture, p.100, in the author manuscript dated 21 August 2024 (126 pp., the journal's revision date; SHA-256 b36f4860…813e)
sourceIssues.printed: "Let k be either Z or a field. Let K be a global field over k. Namely, K is a number field if k = Z; K is a function field of one variable over k if k is a field. … Recall that the relative Bogomolov conjecture of [DGH2, Conj. 1.2] asserts that, if dim Y < g, then there is a constant ε > 0 such that Y(L, ε) = {y ∈ Y(K̄) : ĥ_L(ι(y)) ≤ ε} is not Zariski dense in Y."
sourceIssues.correction: Over function fields the statement needs the usual exclusion of the constant part (for instance, that A has trivial trace or that Y is not constant); [DGH2] formulates the conjecture over number fields.
sourceIssues.reason: For a constant abelian scheme A = A₀ ×_k S and a constant subvariety Y generating it with dim Y < g (for example a constant curve of genus > 1 in its Jacobian), the constant points have canonical height 0 and are Zariski dense, so the conjecture as stated fails for function fields. No result depends on the conjecture itself; its function-field instances in Theorem 4.19 are E1. Found by the extraction (item 182).

sourceIssues.locator: §A.1, definition of admissible Green functions, p.102, in the author manuscript dated 21 August 2024 (126 pp., the journal's revision date; SHA-256 b36f4860…813e)
sourceIssues.printed: "The smooth Green's function g_D is called admissible if the hermitian metric on O(D) defined by ‖1‖ = exp(−g_D) is admissible. The condition is equivalent to (i/π) ∂∂̄ g_D = dµ_Ar − δ_D as currents on C."
sourceIssues.reason: Admissibility of a metric on O(D) is defined just above as c₁(O(D), ‖·‖) = deg(D) dµ_Ar, and c₁ of ‖1‖ = exp(−g_D) is (i/π)∂∂̄ g_D + δ_D. The printed equation is the case deg D = 1, for instance D a point. Found by the extraction (item 192).

sourceIssues.locator: §1.6, definition of stable curves, p.16, in the author manuscript dated 21 August 2024 (126 pp., the journal's revision date; SHA-256 b36f4860…813e)
sourceIssues.printed: "The curve is called stable if it is semistable with arithmetic genus g > 1, and any rational irreducible component of C_k̄ intersects other irreducible components at three or more points."
sourceIssues.correction: Count special points on the normalization: every rational component must have at least three points of its normalization lying over nodes, counting both branches of a self-node (the Deligne–Mumford condition). Equivalently, a smooth rational component meets the other components in at least three points, and a rational component with a self-node meets them in at least one.
sourceIssues.reason: The printed condition ignores self-nodes. For example, a rational curve with one node attached at one point to a smooth genus-one curve is a stable curve of genus 2 in the usual sense, but its nodal rational component meets the other component in only one point. The paper uses stable reduction and the moduli of stable curves from the literature, so the intended (standard) notion is clear. Found by the extraction (item 1 and report §8).

review.reason: Confirmed, and the counterexample checks out. The definition is verbatim in the same author manuscript the errata names: I re-fetched it from http://faculty.bicmr.pku.edu.cn/~yxy/preprints/bigness_and_bogomolov.pdf on 23 September 2026 and its SHA-256 is b36f4860cc0f098ef062523e8a5147e8172d1e4e357fc76a63cd7c0d782a813e, reproducing the recorded hash, with the date 'August 21, 2024' on its title page on page 16. The Deligne–Mumford condition counts special points on the normalisation, both branches of a self-node included, which the printed condition ignores. The recorded example is stable in the standard sense and fails the printed one: a nodal rational curve meeting a smooth genus-one curve at one point has arithmetic genus 1 + 1 + 1 − 2 + 1 = 2 > 1, its rational component carries three special points (two branches of the self-node and the attaching point), and it meets the other component only once. Since the paper uses stable reduction and the moduli of stable curves from the literature, the intended notion is the standard one and nothing depends on the printed wording.
